title: Scientific Coalition for UAP Studies Launches $100,000 Campaign to Build Open-Source Camera Stations That Can Detect UAP

SCU Camera Project

WASHINGTON, DC, UNITED STATES, November 16, 2026 /EINPresswire.com/ -- The Scientific Coalition for UAP Studies (SCU), a 501(c)(3) nonprofit research organization, today announced a $100,000 fundraising campaign to develop, build, and scientifically commission six weatherproof, solar-powered camera stations that record the night sky on their own for weeks at a time.

When two or more stations record the same object, the system can calculate its three-dimensional position, speed, and acceleration. Researchers can then determine whether the object’s motion fits a known natural phenomenon or human technology, or whether it cannot be explained by either. The stations are designed to measure illuminated or self-luminous objects in the atmosphere and in low-Earth orbit, up to 1,000 km.

SCU Executive Board Member Robert Powell said that “Too much of the public conversation about unidentified anomalous phenomena rests on single photographs and anecdotes. Standardized instruments, with their performance measured and published, give researchers and the public data they can check for themselves.”

The automated field camera project builds on proof-of-concept work by Prof. Wesley Andrés Watters of Wellesley College and his team, which includes chief software architect Dr. Matthew Szenher. In that work, two cameras operating together have been calibrated and shown to detect, track, and triangulate near-Earth objects of magnitude +5 and brighter. Campaign funds will pay for further development and upgrading, which includes weatherproof, portable enclosures, solar charging, remote wireless access, improved camera, computer, and timing systems, and two to four weeks of autonomous, unattended recording. Prof. Watters and Robert Powell of SCU serve as co-project directors, supported by a team of about a dozen scientists and engineers.

The project plan includes a field trial in the Massachusetts area in July 2027, and two completed systems will be shipped to New Mexico for field work after September 2027. SCU will provide project updates to donors on a quarterly schedule throughout 2027. All hardware designs and software will be published as open source, so any research group can build and use the same system. Data will be released once the team has analyzed it and published a paper.

A donor has committed $30,000 to match new gifts dollar for dollar, starting with the first dollar, until the match is used. This means that $30,000 of new donations before January 1, 2027 will get us $60,000 towards our goal of $100,000.

Donations are tax-deductible to the extent allowed by law. To donate now, or to read the project brochure and watch a video message from Powell, visit: https://explorescu.networkforgood.com/projects/308263-scu-automated-field-camera-project.

About the Scientific Coalition for UAP Studies:

The Scientific Coalition for UAP Studies (SCU) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit research and education organization (EIN: 83-2626051). SCU was founded in 2017, and its mission is the scientific investigation of UAP. Learn more at https://www.explorescu.org.
